detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure: Control-M/EM export with pool binding fields.
• Data: Control-M job status events including `resource_pool` and wait states.
• For directory layout and inputs, see docs/implementation-guide.md.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ensure `resource_pool` extracted from XML/JSON order definitions.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following search (then save as report or alert; tune time range and threshold):

```spl
index=cicd sourcetype="controlm:job"
| where status="Wait Resource" OR status="Wait Host"
| stats dc(job_id) as waiting_jobs, values(resource_pool) as pools by controlm_server
| where waiting_jobs>=10
| sort -waiting_jobs
```

Understanding this search
Resource pools backing up indicate host shortage or mis-sized concurrency limits.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with the Control-M job plan and run history in the job scheduler. Reconcile job and folder names, start and end times, and queue or pool use for a few highlighted jobs.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add to a dashboard, wire alert actions, and document ownership. Suggested view: Single value (waiting_jobs), Bar chart (by pool).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Control-M/EM export with pool binding fields — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=controlm:job into cicd. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`controlm_server, waiting_jobs`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We watch pools and queues piling up, so we add capacity or spread work before one busy pipe blocks a whole class of jobs.
